questions.question: Your background includes accounting across retail, government, and corporate settings. Which transition required you to learn the most, and how did you build competence in unfamiliar rules, systems, or processes?
Have you worked directly with a CPA or in a public-accounting/CPA-firm environment? If not, what do you expect would be different about review standards, client service, and workload?
This is an in-person role in Westlake Village. Are you currently able to work in the office every day and reside within 15 miles of the office, or can you meet those requirements by your start date?
What appeals to you about an in-office accounting and tax role, and how would you use in-person collaboration during busy periods?
What is your current CPA status, if any, and what are your plans regarding licensure or further tax education?
This position relies on QuickBooks. What hands-on experience do you have with QuickBooks, and if it is limited, how would you become productive in it while maintaining the accuracy of client books?

Describe your approach to working in a fully paperless tax and accounting environment. How would you organize source documents, review notes, approvals, and final workpapers so another team member can follow the audit trail?
Which Microsoft applications and functions have you used most in accounting work? Please give an example of a workbook, report, or analysis you created and explain how you checked it for reliability.

Tell me about a time you collaborated with an auditor, operational manager, vendor, or another accounting team to resolve an issue. What did you contribute, and how did you maintain the working relationship?

Describe a tax or accounting project you led from planning through completion. How did you define responsibilities, monitor progress, resolve blockers, and ensure the final work met quality standards?
